subject: Altura Financial DPA — retention carveout, evidence ask, and signature choreography
messages:
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@alturafin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@alturafin.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Altura DPA - initial redlines and retention question

Hi Ben / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Altura is excited about the integration. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's master DPA and attached a marked-up version with a few requests:

- Retention: we asked for a 7-year retention carveout for transaction-level records tied to audit/AML obligations.
- Subprocessors: a more explicit subprocessor notification window (30 days).
- Data residency: we requested an EU-only option for a subset of records (see redline).

I've attached Altura_DPA_redlines.pdf so you can review the exact language. We also need a short SOC 2 evidence pack (last 12 months) and a completed SIG/CAIQ stub. Can you confirm what evidence you can provide?

Appreciate quick turnaround — our procurement team is trying to get this across the finish line next week.

Samantha
Samantha Price
Head of Procurement, Altura Financial
(attachment: Altura_DPA_redlines.pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@alturafin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Altura DPA - initial redlines and retention question

Hi Samantha — thanks for the redlines. We can move quickly on this. High-level:

- Retention: Redwood's standard is a 3-year retention period for customer data; we understand Altura's AML/audit needs. I'll loop in Legal for a limited carveout discussion (see Marissa).
- SOC 2: we can provide our most recent SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and a short controls evidence pack.
- SIG/CAIQ: we maintain a completed SIG spreadsheet; I'll attach the latest export.

I've attached Redwood_DPA-counterproposal.pdf with our suggested language: a 5-year retention compromise, and an EU residency carveout scoped to specific datasets rather than account-level residency. If this is acceptable, we can route to signature.

Next step: Marissa, can you review the retention carveout and advise if the 5-year compromise needs exec sign-off? Karthik — FYI on deal timing / potential discount if we absorb additional compliance burden.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachments: Redwood_DPA-counterproposal.pdf, SIG-v1.9-responses.xlsx)

Subject: Re: Altura DPA - initial redlines and retention question

Ben / Karthik — reviewed the counterproposal. Notes for Altura: 

- Retention: Legal is comfortable with a narrow, documented 5-year retention carveout provided the language is scoped to "transactional audit artifacts required by law" and we include a mandatory deletion certification clause after the third party no longer needs the data for the stated legal purpose. We do NOT want an open-ended 7-year clause.
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days is acceptable if we keep a standard materiality carveout for security patches and emergency subprocessors (we push for 7-day notice in emergencies).
- EU residency: we will accept dataset-level residency controls but need a precise appendix listing the datasets and access controls.

Action items for me: I'll produce a redline that tightens the carveout language and adds the deletion certification. Ben — please confirm whether the 5-year carveout would require an Exec Exception per policy (if Altura insists on anything >5 years). Karthik — if this goes >5y we should surface to leadership for commercial mitigation.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(attachment: legal_notes_retention_20261013.txt)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@alturafin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Altura DPA - proposed compromise and next steps

Hi Samantha — looping back with a suggested path forward after Legal's review.

Proposal summary (attached: Redwood_DPA-counterproposal.pdf - v2):
- Retention: 5-year retention for narrowly defined "transactional audit artifacts required by law" with a deletion certification requirement within 90 days after joint confirmation the data is no longer required.
- Subprocessor notice: standard 30-day notice with emergency exception language preserved.
- EU dataset residency: we will include an appendix template; specifics can be finalized in onboarding.

We have also attached our completed SIG export (SIG-v1.9-responses.xlsx) and can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report via a secure link. (attachments listed)

If Altura accepts the 5-year carveout language, what's the signature routing on your side? We can put the final DPA in DocuSign — who signs (legal or procurement + exec)? If you want exec approval, we can keep the clause conditional on executive sign-off, but that will add 3–5 business days.

We aim to keep this under your timeline; if you need us to escalate to Tyler (SVP Sales) for a limited exception to 7 years we can do that but will need a business justification.

Best,
Ben
(attachments: Redwood_DPA-counterproposal.pdf v2, SIG-v1.9-responses.xlsx)
